headline: 259 passengers stranded as Biman flight stuck in Rome for 7.5 hours
summary: A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Dhaka was unable to take off for London due to technical issues at Rome's Fiumicino International Airport.
details: A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight remained stranded at Rome's Fiumicino International Airport for approximately 7.5 hours, causing significant distress to 259 passengers.
The aircraft had arrived from Dhaka and was scheduled to depart for London after refueling and collecting catering supplies.
However, the flight was unable to take off at its scheduled time due to technical problems, leaving passengers waiting at the airport.
Sources indicate that this London-bound flight previously stopped at Istanbul Airport in Turkey for fuel and catering before the route was changed to Rome.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has not yet provided an official statement regarding the nature of the technical issue, the expected departure time, or the alternative arrangements for the passengers.

headline: 565 workers laid off at Ashulia garment factory due to order slump
summary: Alliance Knit Composite Ltd cites a severe business downturn and lack of purchase orders as the reasons for the mass layoff.
details: Alliance Knit Composite Ltd (AKCL), an export-oriented garment factory in Ashulia, has laid off 565 workers. The company cited a severe business downturn driven by global and domestic factors.

The decision was announced in a notice issued on August 6, with the layoff effective from August 8. The management stated that the reduction in workforce was necessary to ensure the factory's survival and maintain business continuity.

According to the factory's HR manager, Md Mominul Islam, the global economic slowdown has led to a shortage of purchase orders. This has resulted in production stopping early almost every day for several months.
The factory management has stated that all affected workers will receive their legal dues and compensation as per Section 20 of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
Laid-off workers will be given priority for re-employment if production expands or new recruitment becomes necessary in the future.
Some workers, such as sewing operator Md Jiarul Haque, expressed deep worry after learning of their job loss via text message while away from the factory.
However, Rafiqul Islam, president of the Bangladesh Garments and Shilpa Shramik Federation, has called the layoff 'inhumane' and demanded the immediate reinstatement of all affected workers.
